package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url and dynamic-polyfill)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding cdn.polyfill.io)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain transfer to Funnull (Feb 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after a change in domain ownership. The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam sites, affecting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically deployed to all dependent sites and packages.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website embedding the CDN script)
execution_context.file_location: Injected via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"> in website HTML or via npm packages that reference this CDN

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the visitor is using a mobile device by inspecting the user agent, then redirects the browser to a scam site, resulting in user redirection and potential phishing or further malware exposure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs user agent sniffing and forcibly redirects users to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is a classic sign of malicious web activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate polyfill CDN should only provide JavaScript polyfills for browser compatibility, not perform user agent checks or redirect users to unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User agent checks and redirects may be used for mobile-optimized site delivery, but never from a third-party polyfill CDN script.
key_indicators: User agent sniffing for mobile devices
Forced redirection to external, non-affiliated domains
Injected via a widely used third-party CDN

attack_chain.action: Website or npm package embeds the polyfill.io CDN script in their HTML or JavaScript code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded into the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits the affected website, the malicious JavaScript is executed in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mobile users are identified by user agent sniffing.

attack_chain.action: If the user is on a mobile device, the script redirects them to a scam or phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to further attacks, scams, or malware.

behavioral_signatures: Third-party CDN JavaScript performing user agent sniffing and conditional redirection
Unexpected runtime redirection initiated by polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts making network requests to non-polyfill domains
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io in package source code (e.g., create-polyfill-service-url, dynamic-polyfill)
network_indicators: Outbound requests or redirects to scam domains from pages loading cdn.polyfill.io
Any network traffic from polyfill scripts to domains unrelated to polyfill service
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the inclusion of cdn.polyfill.io scripts in web pages or npm package dependencies. Analyze runtime behavior of polyfill scripts for user agent sniffing and redirection logic. Flag any polyfill script that initiates network requests or redirects to non-polyfill domains, especially on mobile devices. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) and Subresource Integrity (SRI) to restrict and verify third-party scripts. Regularly audit dependencies and block or alert on known-compromised CDN domains.
